newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold struggling to attract demand - trade.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold struggling to attract demand - trade.

text.p: Key Indian demand for gold in the Gulf Arab emirate of Dubai has yet to take off despite a favourable mix of falling prices and the second Indian marriage season, bullion traders in Dubai's souk said on Sunday.
After suffering from lacklustre demand during last month's Diwali (Light) festival, souk traders are still waiting for wedding demand to turn around fourth quarter business.
"1996 has already gone. We are now looking at the market for 1997," said one trader who saw little scope for wedding demand to rally the market for the remainder of the year.
India's second marriage season, running from the end of November to February, usually sees an upturn in bullion and jewellery demand as families secure dowries and presents.
"Demand is not very encouraging. On wedding demand there is not much at the moment compared to the last two years," said another trader with links to the Indian market.
Traders also pointed to economic uncertainties in India as dissuading investment in gold.
The arbitrage between Dubai and Bombay was also narrower than recent months, providing another obstacle to trade.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola (TT) bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders on Sunday at 5,095 UAE dirhams ($1,388.28), down nine dirhams from December 8.
Bombay TT bars were quoted at $1,636, an arbitrage at the lower end of a traditional 15-18 percent spread.
The Islamic holy month of Ramadan starting in the middle of January was seen as potentially bullish for the local bullion market in the next quarter.
Jewellery is sometimes bought to celebrate the festival of Eid al-Fitr at the end of the fasting month of Ramadan.
"One can look to that (Ramadan) for some fresh demand," one trader said.
Ten gram gold pieces in Dubai were assessed at 434 dirhams.
International spot gold was last quoted on Saturday at $368.55-$369.05 an ounce, close to three-year lows.
